You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

If stripes are down-left use r+c instead. Horizontal full-row stripes are a special case of periodic completion; infer period and phase from observed row indices, then repeat. Do not assume zeros are background; use all clues to resolve period, axis and phase.', 2), ('arc_task_3b58a624_recolor_matching_component_to_l_template_color', 'ARC task-3b58a624: recolor one object to prominent L color', 'For recurring Continual-ARC task-3b58a624, each demo preserves the grid and recolors one separate object (occasionally a cell/endpoint) to the color of a prominent L-shaped component. Find the marker pattern’s bounding box and its occupied-cell mask. Slide this mask over every in-bounds location of the original grid; whenever every occupied mask position contains 0, recolor those occupied positions to the marker color. Take the union of all hits, preserving all other cells and the original marker. Do not require the mask’s blank positions to match anything. Demonstrated with marker colors 2, 3, and 9; task solved with zero wrong submissions after two demos. Confirmed again on a 25x13 test with marker 5 over background 9: the same rule solved it with no demos or wrong submissions. The marker mask (relative to its 5x4 bounding box, rows top-to-bottom) was `..#.` / `.#..` / `.##.` / `##..` / `..##`; two placements matched. Always test each mask placement against the original grid, then color the union of all matches. Additional validation: this session had a 15x22 grid with background 0/4 and a 5-cell marker stencil `..#` / `.##` / `#.#` (where # is marker color 5). Exact translations over all-zero positions yielded 14 stencil hits (union of 60 new cells); the submission was correct. The same non-rotated, non-reflected translation-only rule held for marker stencils of sizes 4 and 8 in demos.', 3), ('arc_rule_shift_colored_pattern_down_one_row_task_cc5dea9e', 'ARC rule: shift colored pattern down one row (task-cc5dea9e)', 'For ARC task-cc5dea9e, the transformation is to translate every non-background cell down exactly one row, preserving columns and colors, with cells shifted past the bottom edge clipped; the newly vacated top row is background. Demonstration: an 11x12 grid with background 6 and scattered color-1 cells became the same pattern shifted down one row, dropping the original bottom-row cell. Applied to the test 4x7 grid (background 7, color 0), this yields rows: all 7s; then color 0 at column 2; then color 0 at column 1; then color 0 at column 2.', 1), ('arc_task_07f79b91_color_trailing_background_after_horizontal_8_runs', 'ARC task-07f79b91: color trailing background after horizontal 8 runs', 'For task-07f79b91, the grid has a uniform background (demo used 7; test used 0) and rows containing color 8. In each such row, find the rightmost 8 and recolor every background cell to its right through the grid edge as color 1. Preserve all cells up to/rightmost 8, including any gaps before that rightmost 8, and leave rows without 8 unchanged. A fully filled 8 row has no change. Demo validated this: on one fragmented 8 row, cells strictly right of its rightmost 8 became 1; the repeated row already filled with 8s stayed unchanged. Test solved by turning the 0 tail to 1 on two partial horizontal 8 rows.', 1)]
